### ① Derived judgments

Base and tip. PR head `c2b2168a7` is one commit on merge-base `af57dc729`; `origin/main` is now `7cbefa540` and `git diff --stat af57dc729 origin/main -- packages/plugin-report .changeset packages/i18n/src/useDisplayLocale.ts` shows exactly one unrelated file (`.changeset/9309-object-gallery-filter-destination-typed.md`, +35), so the package and the contract file the card cites are unmoved on main and every reading below holds at the tip. The shared working tree's HEAD (`d18322415`) was never used; all readings were taken from `origin/main`, the PR head object, or a detached scratch worktree at the PR head (removed afterwards, registry pruned, shared status 0 lines).

Accept set: WIDENED, and declared as such. The published declarations, read from a real `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-report build` of the PR head (vite-plugin-dts, exit 0), are `formatValue(value: any, field?: ReportField, locale?: string): string` in `dist/formatValue.d.ts` and `exportExcelWithFormulas(report, data, options?: { columns?; filename?; includeAggregationRow?; locale?: string })` in `dist/LiveReportExporter.d.ts`; the base signatures (`git show af57dc729:.../formatValue.ts` line 15, `LiveReportExporter.ts` lines 160-172) had two parameters and a three-key options bag. So a third positional argument and a `locale` key are now accepted where TypeScript previously rejected them (arity error and excess-property check respectively); nothing previously accepted is refused, nothing is retired. That is a widening, not "unchanged", and the PR's own word for it, "purely additive", is the same fact stated from the consumer's side. `Clause-②: yes` with no arm reads as `yes (widening)` under `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs` ("`yes` / `yes (widening)` — a widening. The second spelling is the first, said out loud"), so the declaration matches the measured direction. Every call that compiled before compiles after: both new parameters are optional in the emitted `.d.ts`, and the package's own `type-check` script (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exits 0 at the PR head once its 10-task dependency closure is built (measured in the scratch worktree: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, `TYPECHECK_EXIT=0`; before the closure was built it failed only with TS2307 unresolved workspace modules, a prerequisite failure, not a verdict).

Runtime behaviour for a caller that omits the argument is byte-identical to before. Node v22.22.2 / ICU 78.2 probe, same command for every row: default `1,234.5`, currency `1,234,567`, percent `1,234.5`, Excel `#,##0.00` `1,234.50`, negative `-9,876,543.21`, `1e15` — `en-US` and `en` identical on all six, and `Intl.NumberFormat('en').resolvedOptions().locale` is `en`, an explicit tag, not the machine's. So the default path changed its tag from `en-US` to the contract's `en` without changing one rendered byte for existing consumers, and the PR's "must-not-change" en cases pin exactly that.

Newly exported: nothing reaches the published entry. `src/displayLocale.ts` exports `DISPLAY_LOCALE_LAST_RESORT = 'en'` and `formatNumberInDisplayLocale`; `src/index.tsx` is unchanged (`git diff --stat` between base and head for that file is empty) and contains no `export *`; the built `dist/index.d.ts` export lines name neither symbol (grep count 0), the runtime ESM export list of `dist/index.js` is the same 16 names as before (`formatValue`, `exportExcelWithFormulas`, … and neither new symbol); `package.json` `exports` is `"."` only, so the `dist/displayLocale.d.ts` file that ships under `files: ["dist"]` is not importable through the exports map. The only `displayLocale` text in `dist/formatValue.d.ts` is a `{@link}` inside a doc comment; its sole non-comment lines are the `ReportField` import and the signature. This is intended (the module is the package-private single spelling of the policy) and correctly not declared as an export in the changeset.

`LiveReportExporter`. In-repo callers of `exportExcelWithFormulas` at the head: `git grep` across the tree excluding `dist` finds the README example and the new test only; imports of `formatValue` or `exportExcelWithFormulas` from `'@object-ui/plugin-report'` in other packages: 1 hit (the README) against a control of 12 total imports from the package. So the PR's statement "no in-repo caller" is true. An out-of-repo caller that passes no `locale` gets `locale = DISPLAY_LOCALE_LAST_RESORT` from the options destructure, `formatCellValue` defaults to the same constant, and the cell formats in `en`, byte-identical to the old `en-US` output; the README, JSDoc and changeset all say "omitted, cells format in `'en'`", which is the behaviour measured, not `en-US` and not an absent tag. `exportWithLiveData` routes to `ReportExportEngine`, which formats no numbers (its only locale calls are two `new Date().toLocaleString()` header lines, count 2, untouched, diff stat 0), so no sixth site hides behind the other exported function.

Malformed-tag degradation is real at all five sites and falls to the contract's last resort. All five display sites route through the one guarded function (`formatValue.ts` lines 56, 59, 62, 65 and `LiveReportExporter.ts` line 312 call `formatNumberInDisplayLocale`; `git grep` at head). Raw `toLocaleString` on `'en_US'`, `''`, `'xx-INVALID-!!'` and an over-long private-use tag throws `RangeError` (four of four); `null` throws `TypeError`; the guard's bare `catch` returns `1,234.5` for every one of them, i.e. `en`. `useDisplayLocale.ts` at `origin/main` declares `return locale || language || 'en'` and its docstring names `'en'`, not `'en-US'` and not `undefined`, as the last resort; the constant re-spells exactly that. Two mutations in a second scratch worktree prove the pins bite: restoring the three touched sources to base (blobs `18c12ccca`, `bc0902c7e`, `72fb40de8`; 5 executable `toLocaleString('en-US'` literals back on disk) reds exactly the seven de-side cases ("Failed Tests 7", the dev's figure); restoring the fix and stripping only the try/catch (anchor replaced once, blob `478964547` to `2d191dd49`) reds exactly one case, "degrades a malformed tag to the last resort instead of throwing", with `RangeError: Incorrect locale information provided` surfacing. Green at the PR head: `reportDisplayLocale-10020.test.tsx` 15 passed (15) with blobs `9606691ed` / `bc5029092` / `b82ecb24c` / `478964547` and `git status --porcelain` 0 lines in the same command; whole package `vitest run packages/plugin-report/` 18 files, 206 tests passed, exit 0. One reading outside the PR's claim, stated so nobody mistakes it for covered: a WELL-FORMED but unsupported tag (`xx-YY`) never throws, and `Intl` silently resolves it to the runtime default (measured: resolved `en-US` on this machine), which is the absent-tag outcome; likewise a JS-only non-string such as a number or `{}` coerces to an empty locale list and the runtime default. Both are `Intl`'s own lookup behaviour, identical for `DatasetReportRenderer`'s three existing `useDisplayLocale()` sites, excluded by the `locale?: string` type, and introduced by nothing in this diff; residual, not a defect of the change.

Executable `'en-US'` literals: base `git grep -c "'en-US'" af57dc729 -- packages/plugin-report` gives `formatValue.ts:4`, `LiveReportExporter.ts:1`, plus 5 in the sibling test; head gives `formatValue.ts:1`, `LiveReportExporter.ts:1`, `displayLocale.ts:3`, README 1, tests 17, and every non-test hit at head sits inside a doc comment (`LiveReportExporter.ts:177`, `displayLocale.ts:14/28/31`, `formatValue.ts:33`). The built bundle confirms it: `toLocaleString('en-US'` in `dist/index.js` 0, against a control of 4 `toLocaleString(` calls total. Instrument control in the same command: 116 files in other packages carry the literal at head.

+441 accounted, file by file from the API listing and the diff: changeset 39, README 10, `LiveReportExporter.ts` +21 (import, 10-line option docblock, `locale?` key, destructure default, three-line `formatCellValue` signature, guarded call), `ReportViewer.tsx` +14 (import widened to `useDisplayLocale`, 9-line comment, the hook, three call sites), test 255, `displayLocale.ts` 73 (two exports, the rest docblock), `formatValue.ts` +29 (import, 18-line docblock, three-line signature, four guarded calls); 39+10+21+14+255+73+29 = 441. The only rendered-output change is the intended one: `ReportViewer` in a non-en session now groups per the display locale; en sessions and argument-omitting callers are byte-identical. `useDisplayLocale()` is called at `ReportViewer.tsx` line 115, before the first early return at line 214 (the `if (!report)` at 118 is inside the `handleExport` closure), the hook is provider-safe per its contract, and `@object-ui/i18n` was already a dependency, so no new dependency and no hook-order hazard.

Card and PR claims, checked: five sites (four plus one) at base, true; `DatasetReportRenderer.tsx` resolves `useDisplayLocale()` three times (lines 523, 889, 1229; a fourth grep hit at 1168 is a comment), true; `formatValue` exported from `index.tsx`, true; three `ReportViewer` call sites, true; package 17.6.0 with `publishConfig.access: public` and no `private` field, true; the contract quotation is verbatim against `origin/main`; the "tsconfig.test.json leg lists the new test" claim holds in the `--listFiles` sense only — the file is reached through the glob `src/**/*.test.tsx` (named 0 times, sibling control also 0), not by name. The changeset-presence gate's header confirms it demands a declaration, not a level.

Prior rulings read: locale,display,i18n,report,intl,formatvalue,usedisplaylocale,tolocalestring,optional,parameter,signature,additive (+2 more) → 33 hits; ADR-0061 D4, ADR-0076 D9, ADR-0130 D4, ADR-0020 D4, ADR-0021 D2, ADR-0029 D8, ADR-0057 D5, ADR-0060 D6, ADR-0061 D1. The script was driven by `--terms` because `--card` reads the objectstack board and this card is on objectui; none of the nine named decisions rules on an optional locale parameter of a UI plugin formatter (record search, ISP segmentation, release artefact schema, state machines, report-as-pivot, i18n ownership, roles, CI aggregate, search contract), so no accepted ruling governs or is overturned here.

### ② Semver level

`minor`, and the changeset matches. The change widens a published signature and a published options type without refusing or retiring anything, which is the additive arm; objectstack `AGENTS.md` Post-Task Checklist step 3 says `Clause-②: yes` takes at least `minor`, and objectui's own convention (AGENTS.md 版本号策略, enforced by `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`) forbids `major` in the fixed group and would spell even a breaking change as `minor` with the break stated in the body. `.changeset/10020-report-display-locale.md` declares `'@object-ui/plugin-report': minor`, the package is in the single `fixed` group (`.changeset/config.json`: 1 group, plugin-report present), and its body states "Additive, not breaking" with the omitted-argument default named as `'en'`, which is what was measured. The body carries no `Clause-②:` line; that is objectui's norm (9 of 1789 changesets on `origin/main` carry one, and objectui's no-major gate has 0 mentions of `Clause-②`), and the declaration lives on the two carriers the checker reads, the PR body and the claim comment, both `yes`. A `patch` would have been defensible for a fix, but with a public signature widening, `minor` is the correct floor; nothing in the diff calls for more.

### ③ Boundary flags

No security or permission boundary is touched: no auth, permission, sanitiser or transport code changes; `sanitizeExcelValue` is untouched and the numeric Excel path bypassed it at base exactly as it does now (a negative number could always begin with `-`), so no injection posture moved. Protocol semantics: the change brings five display sites into line with the already-published `useDisplayLocale` contract rather than altering it; no spec key, registry row or `@objectstack/spec` surface is involved, and `@object-ui/core`'s `formatDisplayNumber` is deliberately not adopted because its malformed-tag retry drops the tag (machine locale). Gate strength: nothing is weakened; a guard is added and its pin is proven to bite by mutation. Product trade-off, stated openly by the PR and confirmed here: the optional parameter leaves out-of-repo callers formatting in `en` when they pass nothing, which is byte-identical to the previous `en-US` output, so it is a non-regression with a documented upgrade path (README, JSDoc, changeset) rather than a silent capability loss. Residuals, none introduced by this diff: well-formed unsupported tags and JS-only non-string tags fall to the runtime default through `Intl`'s own lookup, shared with the declared channel's existing consumers; the two bare `new Date().toLocaleString()` lines in `ReportExportEngine.ts` remain, as objectui#9909's shape, untouched as the PR says. Governed surfaces: none in the seven paths (`packages/plugin-report/**`, `.changeset/`).
